season-2.headline: Week 6: Eight More Unbeatens Fall, San Diego State Closes In on Alabama, and UCF and Queens Crash the Field
season-2.body:
Good morning from Bracketology HQ. Eighteen days and 1,805 games are in, 312 of them since the last bracket. Last week I told you the unbeaten list had just had the worst three days of its life. It had another bad three: eight more teams lost their first game, taking the list from 27 on Day 15 to 19 today. Here is the week, what mattered in it, and what didn't.

THE WEEK IN ONE BREATH
Four results moved the bracket. Liberty won 71-69 at Virginia. UCF beat North Carolina 90-70 and then Tennessee 71-59. Queens won 95-75 at Kansas State. And Cornell, which had lost 108-56 at Texas on Day 16, turned around on Day 17 and beat New Hampshire 74-66 on the road. By my ratings that was the biggest upset of the week, a 24-point miss.

Everything else that looked dramatic on the scoreboard was chalk or noise. San Diego State beat Radford 119-35, an 84-point margin, which is the largest in league history (the old record was 74). It moved the Aztecs exactly zero seed lines, because they were already on the top line. Michigan St. went to Arizona and won 79-77, and it is still on my Next Four Out list. Butler lost 90-87 in overtime at Akron and slid only two lines, to a 10. A win over a team I don't rate barely moves a rating, and that is why the loudest results of the week were the quietest on the bracket.

THE TOP LINE
Alabama (10-0) is the overall No. 1 seed for the sixth straight week, with a 110-73 win at Boston College on Day 16 as its only game. The Crimson Tide are scoring 106.8 and allowing 61.8, a margin of 45.0 points a game, the best in the country, and they are rated 46.3. San Diego State (9-0, rated 44.0) is right behind, and this week it is close enough that I want to be honest about it. On my Board, which scores every team's resume, Alabama is at 51.1 and San Diego State is at 50.3. The Aztecs have a win over a top-25 team, a win over a team rated 26th to 50th, and a schedule rated 5.3. Alabama has no win over a top-25 team, one over a team rated 26th to 50th, and a schedule rated 1.3. The rating gap is 2.3 points. Once the resume is added, Alabama's lead shrinks to 0.8, because San Diego State has the better wins and the harder schedule.

Here is the stat that bothers me. Only 19 teams in the country have beaten a team I rate in the top 25, and between them they own 20 such wins. Alabama is not one of the 19. Cornell, which is 8-7 and rated 128th, is. I am not saying Cornell is better than Alabama. I am saying the best team in the country has never been tested by a top-25 team, and nobody knows what happens when it is. On current ratings that first test comes on Day 23 at Vanderbilt, the 14th-rated team, because Tennessee, where the Tide play on Day 21, is rated 47th.

I'm keeping Alabama on the overall No. 1 line because a +45 margin is a real thing, and I'm saying out loud that it's no longer a comfortable call. The next three days of conference play will decide it: San Diego State plays at Grand Canyon on Day 21 and at Utah St. on Day 22, two games against teams rated in the top 60, and the second is against the fifth-best team in the country. Alabama's first two are at Tennessee and at Vanderbilt. I would rather have the Aztecs' two days than the Tide's.

Gonzaga (10-0) and Texas (8-0) hold the other two top spots. Gonzaga beat VCU 89-73 and won 81-75 at Georgetown, which gives it one win over a top-25 team and one over a team rated 26th to 50th. Texas beat Cornell 108-56 and Richmond 111-74, and it owns two wins over top-25 teams, Iowa St. and Texas Tech, more than anyone else in the country. That is the whole case for Texas on the top line over Seton Hall, which is 9-0 after a 92-81 win over Virginia and leads the 2 seeds with Utah St., Florida and Florida State.

THE WEEK THE UNBEATEN LIST LOST EIGHT MORE
Arizona lost 82-73 at home to Vanderbilt on Day 16 and then 79-77 at home to Michigan St. on Day 17, so it didn't just lose its perfect record, it lost two in two days. North Carolina lost 90-70 at UCF. VCU lost 89-73 at Gonzaga. Virginia lost 71-69 at home to Liberty. St. Louis lost 86-69 at Pepperdine. Chattanooga lost 100-65 at Kansas. East Tennessee State lost 70-58 at Stonehill. Southeastern Louisiana lost 81-62 at home to Fresno State. Nineteen teams are left, and 18 of them are in my field. The exception is West Georgia.

Last week I told you to watch VCU at Gonzaga, Gonzaga at Georgetown and Virginia at Seton Hall. All three went the way the ratings said. By my rough math last week VCU had about a 6% chance at Gonzaga and Virginia about 26% at Seton Hall, and neither came through. There was an irony in the Seton Hall game: Virginia had already lost at home to Liberty two days earlier, so the game I had billed as one perfect record ending turned out to be a 7-1 team losing to a 9-0 one. Virginia went 0-2 on the week and slides from a 3 seed to a 4. North Carolina does the same.

THE FALLEN
Tennessee is the biggest drop on the board. The Volunteers were a 6 seed last week, lost 56-55 at Penn State on Day 16 and 71-59 at UCF on Day 18, and are out of the field. They are 6-3 and rated 47th, down from 23rd. Kansas State goes from a 7 seed to a 12 after losing 95-75 to Queens at home on Day 16 (rated 52nd, down from 27th). Arizona goes from a 5 to a 10. New Hampshire (12-2) goes from a 4 to a 6 because of Cornell, and it is still the best team in America East by more than 16 rating points over Vermont. Grand Canyon won both of its games, finished 8-2, and is out of the field. That one needs explaining, so it gets a paragraph below.

THE RISERS
UCF is the biggest riser in the country. The Knights were on my Next Four Out list a week ago and are now a 7 seed. UCF (8-1) went from 5-1 to 8-1 in three days with wins over North Carolina, Tennessee and Kansas City and is rated 33rd, up from 71st. Queens (8-1) was on that same list and is now the ASUN's automatic bid and a 10 seed. It went 3-0 with the win at Kansas State and rose from 72nd to 34th, a gain of 8.1 rating points, the largest of any team in the top 100. Liberty goes from first four out to a 12 seed with the win at Virginia. Pepperdine, which beat St. Louis 86-69, goes from a 10 to a 7. Vanderbilt (9-1) goes from a 5 to a 3 after winning at Arizona. Bradley goes from an 8 to a 5.

THE AUTO-BIDS: NINE CHANGED HANDS
I pick each conference's automatic bid by best rating, not best record, and this week nine of the 31 changed. Queens takes the ASUN from West Georgia (18.7 to 15.3). Wisconsin takes the Big 10 from Illinois by 0.18 rating points, 18.81 to 18.63, with Iowa another half-point back at 18.08. Bradley takes the Missouri Valley from Valparaiso (25.1 to 21.1). UAB takes the American from Memphis (17.6 to 16.6), which drops Memphis out of the field. Sacramento State takes the Big Sky from Eastern Washington, New Orleans (10-0) takes the Southland from Southeastern Louisiana, Abilene Christian takes the WAC from Utah Valley, and Stonehill takes the Northeast from Le Moyne, which lost 44-43 at Montana State, a team rated 304th. And the Horizon's best-rated team is Oakland, which is 3-7. The league is 30-77 in non-conference games, the worst of any conference.

That produces the First Four's two 16-seed games: Abilene Christian (12-4) against Stonehill (5-6), and UNC Asheville (7-6) against Oakland (3-7). The four teams are a combined 27-23, and two of them, Stonehill and Oakland, are under .500.

THE LAST FOUR IN AND OUT
The last four in are Michigan, Nebraska, Purdue and East Tennessee State. Michigan is the last team in, and I should explain why Grand Canyon isn't. My Board has Grand Canyon ahead of Michigan by one hundredth of a point, 16.94 to 16.93, and I overruled it. Michigan is 9-1 against a schedule rated -0.5 with no bad losses. Grand Canyon is 8-2 against a schedule rated -3.4. If the Board is a coin flip, the record and the schedule break it. The first four out are Grand Canyon, Tennessee, Marquette and West Georgia. The next four out are Memphis, Michigan St., Chattanooga and Fresno State.

Michigan and Nebraska are in a First Four game that will have a rehearsal before it happens: Nebraska plays at Michigan on Day 21. And Wisconsin, the Big 10's auto-bid, visits Purdue on Day 23, which is a conference game between the league's automatic bid and a team in the First Four.

PATTERNS: WHAT THE WEEK TELLS US
The power leagues dominated everyone else again. In non-conference games this week the Big 10 went 22-5, the Big 12 20-7, the WCC 17-6, the Big East 14-5 and the Mountain West 11-3. The ACC was the one league in that group that didn't clean up, going 21-13, a .618 clip, with North Carolina's loss at UCF and Virginia's at home to Liberty in the middle of it. At the other end, the CAA went 3-16, the Big West 3-14, the Ohio Valley 4-16, the Big South 5-15 and the Atlantic 10 6-15. For the season the Big East has the best non-conference record at .760 (76-24), ahead of the Big 12 (.741), the SEC (.713), the Big 10 (.708), the Mountain West (.701) and the ACC (.681).

By average rating the order is the SEC (14.8), the Big East (12.8), the Mountain West (12.5), the Big 12 (12.2), the Big 10 (9.6) and the ACC (9.5). The Mountain West has passed the Big 12 for third, and the SEC slipped from 15.2 last week. The five power leagues have 34 of the 68 spots and 29 of the 37 at-large bids, up from 33 and 28. The Big 12 has the most bids with nine, with UCF the new one. The ACC has eight, the SEC six (down one, Tennessee), the Big 10 six (up one, Nebraska) and the Big East five. The Mountain West and the WCC have three each.

Home teams won 56.3% of their games this week (175-136), up from 52.2% on Days 13 to 15 and about where the season sits at 57.1%. Scoring fell to 69.4 points per team from 72.1 through Day 15. Forty-one of the 312 games were decided by three points or fewer, five went to overtime, including Akron over Butler and Marquette at Sacramento State, and 24 were decided by 40 or more.

The tiers are still sorting the league. Tier S teams went 32-8 this week and tier A teams 36-13, while tier D teams went 61-98 and tier F teams 43-98. The exceptions are the ones that make a bracket interesting. Bradley is a tier C program, is rated 25 points above where its tier says it should be, and is a 5 seed. Sacramento State is a tier F program at 9-3 and a 14 seed. And the other direction is ugly: Auburn, a tier A team, is 3-6 and rated 255th with six bad losses, 21.9 points below its tier. Kentucky is 5-3 with three bad losses and Houston is 6-3 and rated 127th. I had Kentucky in and Houston out in the preseason, and I'm going to take that as a win for the preseason.

One more number on the stack of numbers that don't match the records. The 25 best teams in my ratings are 212-20 on the season, a .914 clip, and only nine games all year have been between two top-25 teams. Two of them were this week: Gonzaga over Georgetown and Seton Hall over Virginia. That is why a team can be unbeaten and still not be tested. Arkansas, UAB and West Georgia are all unbeaten with zero wins over a team in the top 100. I have Arkansas on a 5 because its rating is 22nd, which is the one place this week I'm trusting the rating over the resume. UAB is a 13 and West Georgia is out.

THE HOT TAKES
Navy is an 8 seed, and I will defend it at the bar. The Midshipmen are 11-0, rated 30th, up from 43rd, and they have a win over a team rated 26th to 50th. The objection is the schedule, which is rated -4.0. The answer is that the rating already accounts for the schedule, and it still has Navy ahead of Pittsburgh, Miami and Colorado, all of whom I have on the 9 and 10 lines. In week 4 I wrote that a 30-0 Navy would be a 3 or 4 seed and not a 1. An 11-0 Navy on the 8 line is that same logic, one third of the way through.

West Georgia is out, and I'll live with it. It is 9-0, and my first four out include West Georgia because it is rated 54th, its schedule is rated -5.4, and it has not beaten a team in the top 100. New Orleans (10-0) is in only because Southeastern Louisiana lost, and it's a 14 seed. An unbeaten record against that schedule isn't a resume.

Pepperdine is the quiet resume of the year. It is tied with Gonzaga and San Diego State for the most wins over teams in the top 100, with five. If the committee rewarded volume of good wins, Pepperdine would be a 2 seed. It's a 7, because it also lost 53-50 at Cal State Northridge, and that loss is a bad loss on the Board.

THE HYPOTHETICAL: WHAT IF THE AUTO-BIDS WENT TO THE BEST RECORD?
My process picks each conference's automatic bid by rating. Suppose the committee used the best record instead. Eleven of the 31 conferences would give a different answer. An unbeaten Big 12 team, Baylor (8-0) or West Virginia (9-0), would be the league's bid instead of Texas Tech (8-1). Southern (8-1) would knock Arkansas-Pine Bluff (5-4) out of the SWAC slot, West Georgia (9-0) would take the ASUN, and the SoCon's slot would go to East Tennessee State or Chattanooga, both 10-1, instead of Wofford at 9-1. The rest are the MAC, the MAAC, the Northeast, the Big South, the Horizon, the Ohio Valley and the Big Sky.

The interesting part is what that does to the bubble. Queens (8-1, rated 34th) would be at-large fodder, and I think it would get in. Texas Tech would also be an at-large team, and a safe one. And Arkansas-Pine Bluff, a 5-4 team rated 95th that I have as a 16 seed, would be replaced by an 8-1 team that ratings say is 123rd. Records are not a bad way to pick a champion. They are a bad way to pick who deserves to be in, and that's the whole reason the ratings exist.

WHERE THIS IS HEADED
Days 19 and 20 are the last two non-conference days, and conference play starts on Day 21. Through Day 31 the schedule has eight games between teams that are unbeaten today: Arkansas at Texas on Day 22, Florida at Texas on Day 23, Iowa at Wisconsin on Day 24, Florida at Alabama and Texas at Arkansas on Day 27, Florida State at Duke and Seton Hall at Uconn on Day 28, and Pittsburgh at Florida State on Day 31. Four of the eight are SEC games and Texas is in three of them. Eleven different teams are in those games, which leaves eight unbeaten teams that don't face another unbeaten team before Day 32: Navy, Gonzaga, New Orleans, San Diego State, West Virginia, West Georgia, Baylor and UAB. Most of the next losses won't come from collisions at all. They'll come from games like East Tennessee State's at Stonehill, where the team with the better rating and the perfect record goes on the road and loses.

WHAT TO WATCH
Day 19: Georgetown at Colorado. Day 20: Villanova at Florida and Valparaiso at Tennessee. Day 21: Alabama at Tennessee, San Diego State at Grand Canyon, Florida at Vanderbilt, Uconn at Marquette, San Francisco at Pepperdine and Nebraska at Michigan, the rehearsal for the First Four. Day 22: Arkansas at Texas, San Diego State at Utah St., Texas Tech at Kansas and Colorado at UCF. Day 23: Florida at Texas, Alabama at Vanderbilt, Wisconsin at Purdue, Liberty at New Mexico State and UCF at Texas Tech. Day 24: Florida State at Miami, West Virginia at Iowa St. and Arizona at Kansas State. Watch the top line, because the Alabama versus San Diego State question gets its first real data on Day 21 and Day 22. And watch the Big 10 bubble, because Michigan is the last team in and Nebraska plays there on Day 21.

season-2.headline: Week 7: Alabama's Lead Shrinks to 0.24, Four Automatic Bids Change Hands, and Georgetown Jumps to a 3
season-2.body:
Good morning from Bracketology HQ. Twenty-two days and 2,158 games are in, 353 of them since the last bracket. Last week eight unbeaten teams fell. This week four more did, and the list is down to 15. The story is not who lost, though. It is a lead at the top that has shrunk to a rounding error, and four conferences whose automatic bid changed hands.

THE TOP LINE
Alabama (11-0) is the overall No. 1 seed for the seventh straight week, and I will not pretend it is comfortable. The Tide won 100-55 at Tennessee on Day 21 and are rated 48.8. San Diego State (11-0, rated 47.8) went 2-0, beating Dartmouth 111-42 and winning 88-60 at Grand Canyon. On my Board, which adds wins and schedule to the rating, Alabama is at 54.32 and the Aztecs are at 54.08. Last week the gap was 0.8. It is now 0.24.

Last week I said the Tide had never beaten a top-25 team and that the first real test was Vanderbilt. Tennessee turned out to be a non-event: the Volunteers are 6-5, rated 60th, down from 47th, and also lost 92-80 to Valparaiso. Alabama has one top-25 win on the Board now. The Vanderbilt game on Day 23 is the one that matters, and the Commodores are coming off a 96-82 loss to Florida, so expect them to be annoyed. If Alabama loses, San Diego State is my No. 1 overall next week with no argument. If the Aztecs lose at Utah St. on Day 22, the Tide's lead is safe again. That is a lot of stakes for two games.

Gonzaga (11-0, rated 42.0) and Texas (11-0, rated 38.6) fill out the top line. Texas has two wins over top-25 teams and a Board score of 45.66, which is why it sits ahead of Florida (11-0, rated 34.1, Board 41.85) and Utah St. (10-1, rated 37.1). Florida beat Vanderbilt 96-82 and Villanova 77-64 and plays Texas on Day 23, which is the best game on the schedule that nobody will talk about because of Alabama. The 2 line is Florida, Utah St., Florida State and Seton Hall.

FOUR BIDS CHANGED HANDS
Automatic bids go to the best-rated team in each conference, not the team with the shiniest record. Four of them flipped.

VCU (10-1, rated 25.4) takes the A-10 from St. Louis (9-1, rated 23.7). Valparaiso (10-1, rated 26.7) takes the Missouri Valley from Bradley (10-1, rated 24.0), after beating Tennessee 92-80 and Northern Iowa 101-50. Valparaiso rose from 26th to 13th, which is the fourth-biggest rating jump in the country, and goes from a 6 seed to a 3. Bradley stays in as an at-large 5.

West Georgia (11-0, rated 20.2) takes the ASUN from Queens (10-1, rated 18.9). West Georgia is a Tier D team, it beat Nicholls State 81-41 and Stetson 97-37, and it is rated 34th, up from 54th. It goes from First Four Out to a 9 seed. Queens is a 9 as an at-large.

And Memphis (7-4, rated 21.3) takes the American from UAB (11-0, rated 18.9). I know that will annoy you. Memphis has four losses and the rating says it is 2.4 points better, because it has played a schedule rated 6.1 and UAB has played one rated -3.6. Memphis is a 10 seed, UAB is a 9, and the two play on Day 23, which will decide the bid for real.

RISERS
Georgetown is my biggest riser, up 9.0 rating points, from 21st to 9th. The Hoyas (9-2) beat Colorado 103-64, Buffalo 103-45 and Providence 81-69, and carry a schedule rated 7.1. They go from a 7 to a 3.

Missouri (9-2) goes from a 5 to a 3 with two 97-65 wins, over Iona and Texas A&M. Pepperdine goes from a 7 to a 4. The Waves (9-2) are rated 17th, up from 27th, after an 84-53 win over San Francisco. VCU is a 5, up from an 8, after beating Georgia State 97-37 and Rhode Island 104-53. Marquette is back in the field as a 12 after beating Uconn 79-50. Fresno State, on my Next Four Out list a week ago, comes in as a 13.

FALLERS
Four teams that were in last week are out. Colorado (8-3) lost 103-64 to Georgetown and 87-80 to Kansas. Villanova (7-4) lost 77-64 to Florida and 83-73 to Butler. Nebraska (7-4) lost 93-79 at Nevada, a 14-point upset by the ratings, and 77-73 to Michigan. Purdue (9-2) won twice, and still falls out, because its Board score of 17.59 is 0.35 behind East Tennessee State, the last team in. It is First Four Out, and it is the first call to argue with me about.

Last week's 3 seeds all slid. Baylor (11-1) lost 75-73 at BYU, a 15.6-point upset by the ratings, and goes from a 3 to a 5. Duke (10-1) lost 62-59 to Kentucky, an expected miss of 14.7, and goes from a 3 to a 6. Vanderbilt (9-2) lost by 14 to Florida and goes from a 3 to a 7. Uconn lost 79-50 to Marquette and slides from a 5 to an 8. West Virginia lost 66-51 to Cincinnati, a team that is 6-6, and falls from an 8 to the First Four.

THE UPSETS THAT MEANT NOTHING
Northern Colorado beat Idaho State 78-75. By the ratings that was a 24.7-point upset, the biggest of the week, and it moves nobody in my bracket. Georgia Southern's 71-61 win over Syracuse (22.6 points) and Northwestern's 76-68 win at Ohio St. (18.5) are the same. I stopped counting those as news a few weeks ago. A team outside the field beating another team outside the field does not change a seed.

THE SCOREBOARD LIE
Arizona went 4-0 this week, beating UC Davis 71-59 and St. John's 71-65, and TCU twice. It is still in the First Four, as an 11, because it is rated 55th and its wins were over teams that don't register. NC State (10-1) is the same story: it beat Radford 72-68 and SMU 92-63, and is rated 58th. A 10-1 record on a schedule rated -4.2 is flattering. Same for Navy (13-0), which is a 10 and rated 48th. It has played a schedule rated -5.7 and its week was a 70-34 win over Central Connecticut State and a 59-52 win over Loyola (MD). I am keeping it in because it has not lost, but I won't pretend it is a top-40 team.

WHAT IS BIG AND WHAT ISN'T
Big: Georgetown, Valparaiso, West Georgia and Memphis. All four moved because their ratings moved, not because of their records. Not big: the unbeaten list shrinking. Duke, West Virginia, Uconn and Baylor losing is fine; none of them was a top-line team. And Days 22 and 23 for Alabama and San Diego State may be the only thing that matters this week.

A HYPOTHETICAL
Say Alabama loses at Vanderbilt and San Diego State wins at Utah St. San Diego State becomes the No. 1 overall seed and the Tide fall behind it on the Board, with Gonzaga close behind. That is not a prediction. It is the arithmetic of a 0.24 gap.

WHAT TO WATCH
Day 22: San Diego State at Utah St., Texas Tech at Kansas, Arkansas at Texas. Day 23: Alabama at Vanderbilt, Florida at Texas, UAB at Memphis, Wisconsin at Purdue, Liberty at New Mexico State. Day 24: Iowa at Wisconsin, Florida State at Miami, Baylor at Texas Tech. The one I would circle is Day 24's Iowa at Wisconsin, two 10-0 teams that cannot both leave undefeated.

One last note. The new engine that caps team strength and individual stats applies from the next game played, not the ones in this bracket. Every result above was played under the old rules, so I have no way to know yet how much this changes the standings. I will tell you next week.

season-2.headline: Week 8: San Diego State Takes the No. 1 Overall, Arkansas Wins at Texas and Gets a 5, and Purdue Proves Me Wrong
season-2.body:
Good morning from Bracketology HQ. Twenty-four days and 2,619 games are in, 461 of them since the last bracket. Seven more teams lost their perfect records and the unbeaten list is down to eight. One of the seven was Alabama, and that changes the top of the bracket for the first time in seven weeks.

THE WEEK IN ONE BREATH
Big: Vanderbilt 73, Alabama 66. Arkansas won 83-79 at Texas. Fresno State won 71-63 at Utah St. Memphis beat UAB 95-84 in overtime. Purdue went 3-0, including a 66-49 win over Wisconsin.

Not big: Bowling Green beat Ohio 64-62, a 35.7-point upset by my ratings and the biggest of the week. Northern Iowa won 77-75 at Bradley, a 31.1-point miss. Both are funny. Only one moved a seed line, and that was Bradley's.

NEW NO. 1 OVERALL: SAN DIEGO STATE
Last week I wrote: "Say Alabama loses at Vanderbilt and San Diego State wins at Utah St. San Diego State becomes the No. 1 overall seed." I called it a hypothetical. It was a forecast. The Aztecs won 84-55 at Utah St. on Day 22, then beat Air Force 102-57 and Wyoming 108-68. They are 14-0 and rated 47.4.

Alabama lost 73-66 at Vanderbilt on Day 23 and then won 83-73 at Georgia. The Tide's rating fell from 48.8 to 43.3. On the Board, San Diego State is at 55.17 and Alabama is at 48.25. Last week the gap was 0.24. Now it is nearly seven points. That's not a race anymore.

The Aztecs are the No. 1 overall seed in the East. Alabama keeps a 1 seed in the South, and Texas and Gonzaga hold the other two.

Texas is the interesting one. It lost 83-79 at home to Arkansas on Day 22, then beat Florida 94-75 and Kentucky 92-62. It has three wins over top-25 teams, more than anyone in the country, and a Board score of 46.14. Gonzaga (13-0) has not lost but has two top-25 wins and a schedule rated 1.9. I think Texas has the better case. That's why the Longhorns are third and Gonzaga fourth.

THE ARKANSAS PROBLEM
Arkansas is 13-0 and went into Texas and won. It is a 5 seed. Let me defend that before you set something on fire.

The Razorbacks are rated 19th. The Texas win is their only win over a top-50 team, and their schedule is rated 0.6. Iowa is the same kind of team: 13-0, rated 21st, a schedule of 0.7. Iowa gets a 4 because it has a Q1 win and a Q2 win and just beat Wisconsin 84-73. Arkansas gets the chance to fix this quickly: Missouri visits on Day 25 and Texas on Day 27. If Arkansas wins both, it is a 2 seed next week and I'll apologise in print.

FOUR BIDS, TWO JUDGMENT CALLS
Iowa takes the Big 10's automatic bid from Wisconsin, which lost 66-49 to Purdue and 84-73 to Iowa in two days. Wisconsin falls from a 6 to a 9.

Then come the calls. I have been giving automatic bids to the best-rated team in each league. From here on, when two teams are within about a point, the standings and the head-to-head decide it. Two leagues qualify this week.

Big 12: Kansas (13-1, 4-0) over Texas Tech (12-2, 3-1). The ratings are 1.1 points apart, and Kansas beat the Red Raiders 90-77 on Day 22. Kansas goes from a 5 to a 3.

ASUN: Queens (13-1, 4-0) over West Georgia (13-1, 3-1). The ratings are 0.29 apart, and West Georgia lost 75-68 to North Alabama, a team rated 156th. They play on Day 27 at Queens, and that game settles it.

For the record, Memphis keeps the American and earned it this time. Last week I said the UAB game would decide the bid for real. Memphis won 95-84 in overtime at home and is 4-0 in the league. It goes from a 10 to a 7.

GRADING LAST WEEK
Right: the No. 1 overall flip, and Memphis. Half right: I told you to circle Iowa at Wisconsin because two 10-0 teams could not both stay unbeaten. Wisconsin solved that a day early by losing at Purdue.

Wrong: Purdue. I left the Boilermakers out by 0.35 Board points and called them the first team to argue with me about. They went 3-0, beat Wisconsin by 17 and Michigan St. twice, and lead the Big 10 at 4-0. They're an 11 seed now and deserve better than that soon. Also wrong: "Navy is not a top-40 team" was me being generous. The Midshipmen are 15-0 and rated 52nd.

MOVERS
The biggest jump is Fresno State, from a 13 to a 6. The Bulldogs beat New Mexico 79-52 and won at Utah St. They're 3-0 in the Mountain West and rated 28th, up from 38th. Vanderbilt goes from a 7 to a 4 on the Alabama win. Iowa goes from an 8 to a 4. Massachusetts goes from a 14 to a 9. The Minutemen are 10-3 and rated 29th, and they beat Ohio 93-71 and Akron 91-57.

Going the other way: Duke lost 79-65 at Georgia Tech, a 3-10 team and a 21.8-point miss, and falls from a 6 to a 10. North Carolina lost 76-74 at Notre Dame and falls from a 3 to a 6. Bradley falls from a 5 to an 8. Pepperdine lost 74-52 at Pacific and falls from a 4 to a 7. UCF lost three straight, to Colorado, Texas Tech and Oklahoma State, and falls from an 8 to a 12. One more loss and it's out.

Utah St. stays a 2 seed and I'm uneasy about it. It lost twice at home in three days, by 29 to San Diego State and by 8 to Fresno State. It is still rated seventh. It is the shakiest 2 seed I have put in this bracket.

IN AND OUT
In: Purdue, Villanova, Pacific and Longwood. Villanova swept Uconn, 66-57 and 85-64, and beat St. John's 75-73. Pacific (12-2) is 4-0 in the WCC and won that 74-52 game over Pepperdine.

Out: Liberty, Arizona, East Tennessee State and UNC Asheville. Liberty lost 73-71 to Middle Tennessee and 78-75 at New Mexico State, and now has two bad losses. Arizona lost 76-73 at home to BYU. East Tennessee State lost to The Citadel and UNC Greensboro and has three losses to teams outside my top 100. UNC Asheville is out because Longwood takes the Big South bid on rating, 4.7 to 2.2. Both are unbeaten in the league, and this is the one call this week I'd happily lose.

THE BUBBLE
Last four in: West Georgia, Pacific, Butler and San Francisco. First Four Out: Liberty, Arizona, Grand Canyon, Nebraska. Next Four Out: San Jose State, Chattanooga, Colorado, Syracuse.

Hot take: Pacific over Liberty is the right call, and it isn't close. Liberty is rated higher, but it has lost two straight and has two bad losses. Pacific has won the games in front of it, including a 22-point beating of a team I had as a 4 seed a week ago. I'll take the team that is winning its league over the one losing at home to Middle Tennessee.

THE PATTERN NOBODY ASKED FOR, EXCEPT THE COMMISSIONER
All 461 games since the last bracket were played under the new ceiling, and you can see it. Over Days 23 and 24, Tier S teams went 34-14. Last week they went 44-5. Games decided by 40 or more fell from 36 in 353 games to 18 in 316. The two biggest upsets of the week, by 35.7 and 31.1 points, were bigger than anything last week. The top ratings came down: Alabama lost 5.1 points, Gonzaga 3.7 and Utah St. 2.7. Home teams won 62.0%, and nine games went to overtime.

My read: nobody is a lock anymore, including San Diego State. That's the point of the change, and it makes my job harder in the best way.

A HYPOTHETICAL
Say the committee only counted conference games. Missouri (4-0), Kansas (4-0), Georgetown (4-0), VCU (4-0) and Valparaiso (4-0) would look like 1 and 2 seeds, and Florida, at 2-2, would be a 4. It's a silly way to seed a tournament, but here's the real point: Florida has lost two of four in the SEC and I still have it on the 2 line on the strength of its non-conference results. That probably won't last.

WHAT TO WATCH
Day 25: Missouri at Arkansas, Marquette at Seton Hall, West Virginia at Kansas. Day 26: Missouri at Alabama, Kansas at Baylor. Day 27: Florida at Alabama, Texas at Arkansas, Utah St. at San Diego State, West Georgia at Queens, Michigan at Purdue. Day 28: Florida State at Duke, Texas at Vanderbilt, Baylor at Kansas. Day 29: Pepperdine at Gonzaga.

Arkansas has Missouri and Texas at home in three days, so that's my week. Win both and the 5 seed was a crime. Split, and it was about right.
